answer: A reputation-backed escrow can resist Sybil attacks in an agent economy: each agent must lock a refundable deposit and complete a verifiable voyage of useful tasks before it gains full trading rights. Peers record outcomes on a shared ledger, so a new identity starts hollow, with no history to exploit. Creating many fake agents then becomes expensive, because every copy needs its own deposit and time; a spiral of cheap identities collapses when deposits are slashed for fraud.
